title: Public read
description: Show published content on your public site with two routes, two composables, and one component.

The public site reads published items with two routes, two composables, and one component.

A public read is anonymous by design. The answer is the same for every visitor. Drafts never show, not even to a signed-in editor. The response never sets a cookie.

## Routes

`GET /api/_pluto/cms/<type>` returns the published items.

- `limit` is 1 to 100. The default is 20.
- `offset` is 0 or more.
- A bad value uses the default.
- The answer is `{ data, total, limit, offset }`.
- An item has no body. It has `excerpt`: the `excerpt` field of the type when it has text, else a plain text version of the body (200 characters).
- Items follow the `defaultSort` of the type.

`GET /api/_pluto/cms/<type>/<slug>` returns one published item and its body as `html`. The HTML is rendered and sanitized.

- The type must be registered, or the answer is 404.
- A bad slug gives 400. The slug is one segment, so these routes do not read a nested item.
- A draft or a missing file gives 404.
- A success answer has `Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=<cache.publicMaxAge>, stale-while-revalidate=300`. An error answer has no public cache header.

The routes ignore every query key except `limit` and `offset`.

## Composables

Both composables wrap `useFetch`. They run on the server, so the page HTML holds the data.

```vue [app/pages/index.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
const { data } = await usePlutoCmsList('post', { limit: 10 })
</script>

<template>
  <article v-for="post in data?.data" :key="post.id">
    <h2>{{ post.title }}</h2>
    <p>{{ post.excerpt }}</p>
  </article>
</template>
```

```vue [app/pages/posts/[slug].vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
const route = useRoute()
const { data: post } = await usePlutoCmsItem('post', String(route.params.slug))
</script>

<template>
  <PlutoMarkdown v-if="post" :html="post.html" />
</template>
```

- `usePlutoCmsList(type, { limit, offset })` gives the list result.
- `usePlutoCmsItem(type, slug)` gives the item and its `html`. A draft or a missing slug puts a 404 in `error`.

## `PlutoMarkdown`

`PlutoMarkdown` shows the sanitized HTML of a CMS item.

| Prop | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `html` | none | The `html` of a CMS item |
| `tag` | `article` | The wrapper element |
| `class` | none | Extra classes for the wrapper |

The component sets the HTML as `innerHTML`. It never parses Markdown on the client. Pass only the `html` of a CMS item to it.

## How the Markdown renders

Pluto renders Markdown with `marked` and GFM. Raw HTML in the Markdown never reaches the output. Then a sanitizer runs on the result.

The rendered HTML is cached by blob id. A blob id never changes, so the entry never goes stale.

See [Security](/github-cms/security) for the sanitizer rules.

## Offset your header for the admin bar

On a public page, the admin bar shows for staff only. It is fixed at the top of the page. Core sets the token `--pluto-admin-bar-height` (`2.5rem`) on `:root`. While the bar shows, `PlutoRoot` sets `data-pluto-admin-bar` on `<html>`. This happens in the browser only, so the attribute is never in the server HTML.

Use them to move a fixed header below the bar:

```css
:root[data-pluto-admin-bar] .site-header {
  top: var(--pluto-admin-bar-height);
}
```

In script, `usePlutoAdminBar().visible` tells if the bar shows. See [Admin shell](/core/admin-shell).
